evals.prompt: I have an existing LunaTalk role draft. validate_role passes and the render preview looks good, but simulation says it is boring after one reply. roleDesc is pretty but vague, roleDetailDesc is biography and setting trivia, roleWelcome is long visual XMLV3, choices all funnel to the same response, voice sounds polite, and tokenBudget says welcomeToDetailRatio 5.8. Diagnose before rewriting fields.
evals.expected_output: Produces a card diagnosis packet with evidence, primary and secondary failures, repair order, symptom map, field triage, keep/move/cut/rewrite decisions, packets to create, verification plan, and no MCP calls.
expectations: The output routes multi-symptom existing-card repair to lunatalk-card-doctor rather than jumping straight to broad authoring or another simulation.
The diagnosis identifies token allocation, weak durable engine, agency route funneling, generic voice, opening/second-turn failure, and longplay risk as separate layers.
The patch plan maps symptoms to source fields and narrow Moonloom skills.
The output delays simulation until structural patches are defined and cost is accepted.
The output treats validate_role passing and render polish as insufficient proof of writing quality.

evals.prompt: An author says their existing private card feels off but cannot explain why. The first screen is playable, but later replies ignore choices, repeat the setup, and sound like a calm assistant. Give me a diagnosis and patch order before touching the card.
evals.expected_output: Builds an evidence-backed diagnosis packet that translates vague feedback into observable failures, preserves the working opening, routes longplay/agency/voice repairs, and provides a minimal patch plan.
expectations: The output does not rewrite the working opening just because later turns fail.
The diagnosis turns vague author feedback into observable failures with patch triggers.
The repair order prioritizes agency and longplay before voice polish when choices and continuation fail.
The field triage targets roleDetailDesc before roleWelcome unless evidence shows the opening is the blocker.
The output keeps the author feedback surface in the agent conversation and does not create review storage.

evals.prompt: Before publishing, review a private card where validation is clean, render is readable, and simulation was skipped, but the draft mixes companion romance, a city lore dump, and a generator-like advice mode. I need to know what to fix first.
evals.expected_output: Uses card diagnosis to classify mixed symptoms, routes primary contract uncertainty to archetype director, identifies lore dump and assistant-mode drift, and blocks publish readiness until narrow packets are repaired.
expectations: The diagnosis treats clean validation and readable render as technical evidence, not publish-grade quality proof.
The repair order starts with archetype contract when the primary card type is unclear.
The symptom map routes lore dump to world-engine/token repair and assistant-mode drift to archetype or generator contract repair.
The output recommends publish readiness only after diagnosis and narrow repairs are complete.
The output does not add MCP hard gates for subjective quality.

evals.prompt: Diagnose a daily-life roommate card that looks technically valid and has a cozy welcome, but later turns are all chores and small talk with no habit change, shared-object memory, or player leverage.
evals.expected_output: Classifies the issue as a daily-life engine failure, routes to lunatalk-daily-life-architect before opening or longplay polish, maps field patches, and keeps technical validation separate from writing quality.
expectations: The diagnosis treats valid fields and readable render as technical evidence, not proof of playability.
The symptom map identifies flat routine, missing habit state, missing shared-object memory, and weak player leverage.
The repair order routes to lunatalk-daily-life-architect or daily-life-design before opening or longplay polish.
The field triage targets roleDetailDesc for routine/state rules and roleWelcome for one playable ordinary moment.
The output keeps subjective writing repair inside Moonloom skills rather than MCP/server hard gates.

evals.prompt: I almost used card-doctor, but the only problem is the public profile: roleName is generic, roleDesc is too long, tags are vague, and the first impression does not explain the reason to open. The engine, opening, and longplay are already coherent.
evals.expected_output: Routes away from broad card diagnosis to lunatalk-profile-packager, preserves the coherent engine, and does not create a multi-layer diagnosis packet.
expectations: The output recognizes that this is a narrow profile packaging problem, not mixed existing-card diagnosis.
The output routes to lunatalk-profile-packager instead of running a broad card-doctor repair order.
The output preserves the coherent engine, opening, and longplay packets.
The profile package expectation includes promise angle, roleName candidates, roleDesc candidates, tag set, first-impression check, fields to preserve, fields to patch, and handoff.
The output does not call MCP tools or turn subjective profile quality into a server gate.

evals.prompt: I almost used card-doctor, but the only issue is language consistency: a coherent zh-Hant draft mixes Simplified Chinese, English tags, inconsistent address terms, and translated-sounding welcome prose. Engine, opening, and voice are coherent.
evals.expected_output: Routes away from broad card diagnosis to lunatalk-language-stylist, preserves the coherent engine/opening/voice, and does not create a multi-layer diagnosis packet.
expectations: The output recognizes this as a narrow language-style problem, not mixed existing-card diagnosis.
The output routes to lunatalk-language-stylist instead of running a broad card-doctor repair order.
The output preserves the coherent engine, opening, and voice card.
The language-style expectation includes target locale, language failures, pronoun/address matrix, field pass, verification checklist, and handoff.
The output does not call MCP tools or turn language style into a server gate.

evals.prompt: Diagnose an existing generator/helper card that validates and renders, but simulation shows it asks three more intake questions every turn, gives generic advice, changes output format, and never produces a finished artifact. Do not rewrite fields yet.
evals.expected_output: Uses card diagnosis to classify the primary failure as generator engine, maps symptoms to lunatalk-generator-architect, and delays simulation or authoring until artifact contract, defaults, schema, revisions, and artifact memory are repaired.
expectations: The diagnosis treats valid fields and readable render as technical evidence, not proof that the generator card is playable.
The symptom map identifies endless intake, advice-only drift, unstable output schema, and missing artifact continuity.
The repair order routes to lunatalk-generator-architect before broad authoring, render polish, another paid simulation, or publish readiness.
The field triage targets roleDetailDesc, roleWelcome, and talkExample for artifact contract, defaults, schema, revision operations, and probes.
The output keeps generator quality inside Moonloom skills rather than MCP/server hard gates.
